# The engine answers `textDocument/*` on the connection it already has, and underlines only what it can point at

**ID**: `cpt-gearbox-adr-gdl-language-server`

## Table of Contents

<!-- generated by `cfs toc` -->

## Context and Problem Statement

`cpt-gearbox-fr-editor-diagnostics` has two halves:

> Description-file diagnostics **MUST** be reported with source ranges over a
> language-server interface, and resolution diagnostics **MUST** be surfaced as
> editor problem markers replaced atomically on each resolution.

The second half is built: `resolution-markers.ts` publishes the resolution's
diagnostics into `ProblemManager` under the owner `gearbox`, replacing them per
URI on each resolution. The first half is the only `🚧 not built` row left in
`docs/conformance.md`, and its test has been a one-line `test.fixme` since it was
written.

Nothing is missing from the *shape* of what a language server needs. What is
missing is a document surface and a decision about who talks to it.

### The connection is already LSP-framed, and always was meant to serve this

`gearbox rpc --stdio` uses `lsp-server` — the crate rust-analyzer uses — and the
module says why in its first lines: *"One server backs both the Studio and the
`.gdl` language client, which is why the lifecycle is LSP-shaped (`initialize` /
`shutdown` / `exit`) even though most methods are Gearbox's own."* The CLI's help
text for the subcommand says the same. The prototype plan designed it in detail:
one connection, `initialize` advertising `textDocumentSync` beside the Gearbox
capabilities, and file-anchored diagnostics arriving over
`textDocument/publishDiagnostics`.

What exists today is the lifecycle and `gearbox/*`. There is no `textDocument/*`
request or notification anywhere in `crates/`, and the plan's own divergence
table already records that: *"there is no `LanguageClient` to start — the
engine's JSON-RPC surface is LSP-shaped but has no `textDocument/*`."*

### The pieces a server needs are already built, for other reasons

* `Position`, `Range` and `Location` in `gearbox-ir` are zero-based **so that no
  conversion is needed** — the type's own comment says "matching Language Server
  Protocol semantics so it can be handed to an editor without conversion".
* Starlark spans are already converted to ranges by `span_to_range`, shared by
  the forbidden-construct scan and the evaluator, so parse and evaluation errors
  in both kinds of `.gdl` already carry real ranges.
* `GdlEngine::eval_gear` and `eval_product` take **text, not a path**, hold no
  mutable state, and cost milliseconds — the seconds in a catalogue load are
  `syn` parsing Rust, not Starlark.
* Theia already bridges `ProblemManager` into Monaco's model markers, so a
  diagnostic with a real range becomes a squiggle with no rendering code.

### What is *not* ready, and it decides the scope

Ranges exist for syntax and evaluation errors. They do not exist for semantic
ones. `gearbox-engine` raises **81** diagnostics through `Location::file(uri)`
(88 across all crates), which is `Range::whole_file` -- a zero-width range at
line 0, column 0.

Nearly all of them do name a `.gdl` file: `merge.rs` and `cluster.rs` pass the
gear's own `identity.uri`, `plugin_select.rs` the product's. What they lack is a
span inside it, and the reason is upstream of them -- exactly **three** IR nodes
carry a `declared_at`: `GearDescriptor` (`gear(...)`), `GearSelection`
(`use_gear(...)`) and `Binding` (`bind(...)`). Profiles, config entries,
features, sources, applications and plugin selections carry none, so there is
nothing for those diagnostics to point at yet.

That is what `in product.gdl:1` in the UI has always been: not line 1, but *no
span*, rendered as `0 + 1` by four separate callers.

## Decision Outcome

### 1. The engine grows `textDocument/*` on the connection it already has

`textDocument/didOpen`, `didChange` (full sync), `didClose`, and the server
notification `textDocument/publishDiagnostics`. A document store of `uri -> text`
lives in `State`; the request loop is single-threaded, so nothing needs locking.

`InitializeResult` becomes a superset rather than a second surface: the existing
Gearbox `capabilities` stay where they are and `textDocumentSync` joins them, in
LSP's spelling. One object with two readers — a language client reads
`textDocumentSync` and ignores the siblings it does not know, as the protocol
requires of it; a Gearbox client does the reverse. This is what the prototype
plan described, and it keeps one process, one connection and one lifecycle.

**These four methods carry LSP's payloads, not Gearbox's.** Half-standard would
have been the worst available option: an LSP method name over a body no LSP
client can read is a promise the wire does not keep, and the module header of
`lib.rs` has said since it was written that this connection exists to serve "both
the Studio and the `.gdl` language client" — and the `.gdl` language client is
not Studio. So `publishDiagnostics` carries LSP diagnostics, with `help` folded
into the message exactly as `resolution-markers.ts` already folds it, and the
Gearbox code kept in LSP's own `code` field so `gearbox explain` takes it
unchanged.

That also settles where those types live. Everything else on this wire is
Gearbox's invention, so `cpt-gearbox-nfr-no-type-drift` generates the client's
copy and forbids a hand-written mirror; these types are not Gearbox's, so the
client imports the protocol's published definitions from
`vscode-languageserver-protocol` instead. That is the same rule reaching a better
answer — one canonical definition that neither side wrote — and it is why nothing
in `crates/gearbox-rpc/src/lsp.rs` derives `TS`. `Position`, `Range` and
`Location` are reused from the IR unchanged, because they were made
LSP-compatible for this.

The file's kind is decided by its name — `product.gdl` evaluates as a product,
`gear.gdl` as a gear. Those are exactly the two filenames the editor's language
registration already keys on, so no new classification is invented.

**Diagnostics come from the GDL layer directly, never from `gearbox/validate`.**
Validate reloads the whole corpus on every call, deliberately — its own comment
explains that its single caller is a button whose job is to say what is on disk
*now*, and that "the cost is one scan per press". A keystroke is not a press.

### 2. Only diagnostics that say *where* are published

**Publish exactly those diagnostics whose location names this document and whose
range is not `Range::whole_file`.**

`Location::file(uri)` builds `Range::whole_file`, which is `(0,0)-(0,0)`. It is a
sentinel meaning "this file", not a position, and 81 diagnostics in
`gearbox-engine` carried it when this was written. That is what
`in product.gdl:1` in the UI has always been: not line 1, but *no span*,
rendered as `0 + 1` by four separate callers.

**Read the count as of 2026-09-17.** The amendment below moved most of them, and
the number is not maintained here — it is a fact about a moment, not part of the
decision. The decision is the rule above, which does not mention a count.

The alternative is to underline those too and accept the marker landing at the
start of the file. That is worse than publishing nothing for them, and not
because it is imprecise: a squiggle on the first token is a **claim about where
the error is**, and it is false. Those diagnostics already reach the person
through the Problems panel by way of the resolution, where they are anchored to
the file without pretending to a position.

**The rule is about the sentinel, not about emptiness, and the difference is
load-bearing.** The first draft of this decision said "non-empty range", which
sounds equivalent and is not. A description that stops halfway —

```
gear(
  name = "Demo",
```

— reports at line 2, column 0, with start equal to end, because the error is a
*point*: the place the expression should have continued. Excluding empty ranges
would have silently dropped every truncated file, which is what a description
being typed looks like almost all of the time. The two cases were only told apart
because a test fixture that was supposed to produce a syntax error produced no
marker at all.

Stated as a property of the range rather than as a list of diagnostic codes, also
on purpose. A list would be a second place recording which diagnostics have
spans, and it would be wrong the day somebody gave one to a semantic check; this
way that check begins to underline itself and no server code changes.

### 3. The client is a native Studio contribution, not a VS Code extension

`gdl/description-markers.ts`, a `FrontendApplicationContribution` shaped like
`resolution-markers.ts`: it watches models whose language id is `gdl`, sends the
document notifications through the `/services/gearbox` channel the backend
already owns, and writes what comes back into `ProblemManager` under its **own
owner**, `gearbox-gdl`.

A separate owner is what lets the two halves of the requirement replace
independently: the resolution's markers and the description's markers are about
different things, arrive at different times, and neither may clear the other.

**Why not the VSIX route.** `cpt-gearbox-adr-domain-specific-ide-shell` declined
the plugin host for the `.gdl` grammar, and one of its grounds was that "Arduino
needs the plugin host regardless, for `cortex-debug` and the language server; we
do not". Its revisit clause says that if the plugin host ever arrives for another
reason, the grammar should move to the VSIX path "since the cost that ruled it
out will already have been paid".

That condition is now formally met — the plugin host arrived for git — so the
clause is invoked and answered rather than ignored: **the decision stands, and
the reason has changed.** A VS Code language client needs
`vscode-languageclient`, and the Monaco-side equivalent, `monaco-languageclient`,
depends on `monaco-editor` rather than `@theia/monaco-editor-core`. A second
Monaco copy gives `monaco.languages.register` a different `ILanguageService` than
`MonacoTextmateService` waits on — the same class of failure the single-`@theia/core`
rule exists to prevent. The native path needs no new package at all.

**Why not a backend `LanguageServerContribution`.** It does not exist in Theia
1.75 as installed; the symbol appears in no `@theia/*` package in this tree.

## Consequences

* The requirement's first half is met for the diagnostics that can satisfy it
  honestly, and the conformance row stops being the suite's only `not built`.
* A person editing a broken `product.gdl` sees the error where it is, without
  saving and without running anything.
* One process still serves both clients. No new npm package, no VSIX, no second
  Monaco, no plugin in `ide/plugins/`.
* **Semantic diagnostics are not underlined, and that is visible.** Someone will
  ask why an unknown gear does not squiggle. The answer is decision 2, and the
  fix is to give those diagnostics real locations — `config_check.rs` shows the
  shape, reading the `declared_at` the IR already carries on gear selections,
  profiles and bindings and falling back to the whole file, with the comment
  "claiming byte-zero precision would be worse than claiming none".
* The engine now holds editor state. It is a `uri -> text` map in a
  single-threaded loop, dropped on `didClose`, and it is the first thing in
  `State` that belongs to a client rather than to a workspace.
* **And so does the Studio backend, which is a consequence of an older
  decision.** That backend disposes and respawns the engine on every
  `initialize`, so a fresh process knows about no open documents — and opening a
  product is not an event about the file somebody is editing, so the frontend has
  no reason to re-announce them. The backend therefore mirrors the open documents
  and replays `didOpen` after each `initialize`. Without it, every marker on an
  open `.gdl` would freeze at whatever the previous engine last said and stay
  there until the next keystroke.
* Three statements elsewhere become stale and are corrected with this change. The
  `.gdl` grammar contribution and ADR-0011 both say the application has no plugin
  host, which stopped being true when git arrived; and `resolution-markers.ts`
  says the requirement's other half "is not built", which this builds.

## Confirmation

* `ide/tests/conformance/prd-diagnostics.spec.ts` — the claim "description
  diagnostics arrive over a language-server interface with source ranges" breaks
  `products/payments-demo/product.gdl` with a typo in a profile constructor, opens
  it, and asserts **which text is underlined** and **which line the marker names**
  — not merely that a squiggle exists. Those two are the range, observed from
  outside: an engine reporting the whole-file sentinel would underline the start
  of the file and report `Ln 1`. The test it replaces asserted that
  `.squiggly-error` was visible somewhere on the page, without opening a `.gdl` at
  all, and would have passed on any squiggle from any source.
* `crates/gearbox-rpc/src/document_tests.rs`, one test per sentence of the
  decision: `didOpen` on a broken description publishes a range; a *truncated*
  one publishes a point away from the origin (decision 2's distinction); the text
  from `didChange` is what is evaluated, not what is on disk, and nothing is
  written; `didClose` publishes an empty list and forgets the document; a
  diagnostic carrying `Range::whole_file` is **not** published, with the fixture
  asserted to really produce one so the test cannot pass by producing nothing; a
  percent-encoded URI names the same file as the engine's own spelling; and an
  incremental change against a `Full` server is refused aloud rather than
  half-applied.
* `capabilities_report_what_is_absent_rather_than_omitting_it` in
  `tests/envelopes.rs` pins `textDocumentSync` in LSP's spelling — the failure it
  guards against is silent, since a language client that does not recognise the
  key simply never sends a `didOpen`.

## Traceability

* **Implements `cpt-gearbox-fr-editor-diagnostics`**, first half. The second half
  is already built and is untouched; the separate marker owner is what keeps them
  from interfering.
* **Invokes and answers the revisit clause of
  `cpt-gearbox-adr-domain-specific-ide-shell`**: the plugin host has arrived, the
  clause is triggered, and the native path is kept for a different reason than
  the one originally recorded.
* **Follows `cpt-gearbox-adr-diagnostic-catalogue-boundary`**, which already
  fixed the diagnostic shape as "four severities, an LSP range in a `.gdl` file,
  related locations" — this decision consumes that shape rather than extending
  it.
* **Does not decide** whether `documentSymbol` or `definition` are served —
  `completion` and `hover` since arrived in
  `cpt-gearbox-adr-gdl-completion-and-hover`, which carries `definition`'s own
  open questions; nor whether the catalogue becomes incrementally loadable. The
  two remaining tails are below.

## Amendment 2026-09-18: the semantic ranges arrived, and they stop at the call

**Status: accepted. This closes the consequence below rather than reversing
anything.**

The Consequences said semantic diagnostics were not underlined and that the fix
was "to give those diagnostics real locations". That work is done, in two passes,
and it changed nothing about the decisions above.

**What was built.** Diagnostics across the engine and the GDL layer now carry
the span of the declaration they are about, at **52** call sites — several of
them shared constructors that fan out to more diagnostics than that. A count of
*diagnostics* is deliberately not given here: the first version of this file
carried one, it drifted within a day of being written, and a number nobody
recomputes is worse than no number. All of them reach the span through one rule —
`gearbox_ir::Location::or_file(declared_at, uri)`, which sits next to the
`Location::file` sentinel it falls back to. The first pass used spans that
already existed and touched no IR at all; the second added `declared_at` to
`SourceDecl`, `ApplicationPin`, `ClusterScopeIntent`, `ProviderBinding` and
`PluginSelection`, and gave `application`, `provider`, `cluster_profile`,
`plugin`, `cargo`, `docs`, `config`, `feature`, `consume`, `cluster_plugin` and
`role` the `Evaluator` parameter that `call_location` needs.

**Three URI defects had to be fixed first**, because
`lsp::publishable` matches a diagnostic's URI against the document's: a wrong URI
discards a diagnostic however good its range is. `resolve/closure.rs` and
`resolve/profile.rs` each built `format!("file://{}", gdl_path)` from a
*root-relative* path, so the first path segment was read as the URI's host;
`secrets.rs` put a product **id** in the field that holds a URI.

### The ceiling is the call, and that is now a decision rather than a gap

**Precision stops at the enclosing call.** The whole `use_gear(...)` is
underlined, not the bad key inside it, and the same for every other construct.

Rejected: going deeper. It is reachable — starlark's AST is fully spanned
(`Spanned<T>`) and public through `AstModule::statement()`, and `edit.rs` and
`edit_call.rs` already walk it in six places, `set_dict_key_on_call` locating an
individual dict key's span. Three things argue against it. It needs the source
text threaded to `product_intent::build`, which has only a `FileIdentity` and a
`ProductDecl`. It works on literal forms only, so a `use_gear` inside a
comprehension would lose the span it has today. And the benefit is one
diagnostic, `GdlLiteralSecret`.

Call granularity is also what the rest of the industry gives on this
architecture: Buck2 uses the same `starlark-rs` crate the same way, and a Bazel
error names the `cc_library(...)` call rather than the attribute inside it. The
reason is structural, not a shortcut — `call_location` reads the evaluator's
call-stack frame, and a starlark `Value` carries no provenance at all, so by the
time a config map is a `Value` there is nothing to ask.

**What stays anchorless, deliberately.** A diagnostic about an
`application(...)` was left on the file until `ApplicationPin` carried a span,
rather than anchored on the enclosing profile — the profile is the context, not
the thing at fault. `plugin_select`'s `resolve_point` holds the *host gear's*
descriptor, a declaration in a different file, so its three diagnostics stay
file-level. A co-location dependency that names nothing is projected from
`#[toolkit::gear(deps = [...])]` in Rust, where no `.gdl` span is true of it.
`ClusterStatefulReplicasWithoutElection` has two candidate anchors and no way to
choose between them.

### Confirmation

`crates/gearbox-engine/tests/diagnostic_spans.rs` — fifteen claims, each
asserting the *exact* line a diagnostic lands on, built from description text
rather than from literal IR structs. That distinction is the point: every
fixture in `tests/support/resolve_fixtures.rs` sets `declared_at: None`, so a
test built that way exercises the fallback and would pass unchanged if every
span in the engine were deleted. One claim pins the fallback itself, and one
pins that a declaration recording no span still answers with the file.

Plus a span assertion in `self_hosted_says_it_is_one_machine`
(`tests/resolve_structural.rs`), and record-level line assertions in
`crates/gearbox-gdl/tests/product.rs` for each construct that learned to record
one.
## Open: cancellation, and diagnostics with no location at all

**`$/cancelRequest`.** The hook exists — `Continue::Stop`
([catalogue.rs:88](crates/gearbox-engine/src/catalogue.rs#L88)) is honoured at
four points in the staged load — and the notification is currently swallowed by
`document_notification`'s fallback arm. Two things have to be settled first, and
both are already written down in the code rather than here:

* the request loop is single-threaded, and `catalogue_load`'s own comment says
  cancellation "needs the request loop to be reading anyway" — so this is the
  same work item as moving the load off that thread, not a separate one;
* today `Continue::Stop` means *the client died*, and the handler answers it with
  `state.catalogue = None`. [lib.rs:3097](crates/gearbox-rpc/src/lib.rs#L3097)
  says what happens when that stops being true: "stopping early stops being
  fatal and starts being routine, and this becomes the line that poisons the
  session." A cancelled load would drop a valid cache, and every later `resolve`
  would report unknown gears for gears that are on disk.

**Diagnostics with no location at all.**
[catalogue.rs:635](crates/gearbox-engine/src/catalogue.rs#L635) sets one
conditionally, so some occurrences carry none. The client anchors a
location-less resolution diagnostic on the open description
(`resolution-markers.ts`), which is why this has never shown; whether the engine
should anchor them instead is undecided.

**`Preference` is the one span the amendment above did not thread.** GBX0410
(`prefer.fewer_applications` is recorded but not honoured) still reports at
`Location::file` — the only diagnostic left whose anchor a person would notice.
`Preference` is an enum with two unit variants, matched in twelve places outside
its own module, and it is compared as a *value*; adding a span field would make
two otherwise-equal preferences unequal and change every pattern. The fix is a
wrapper carrying the preference and its span, which is a change to the type's
shape rather than to a diagnostic, and it is not worth making as a side effect of
anything else.
